newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: COLONIAL SPELLS OUT DIVIDEND POLICY.
newsitem.headline: COLONIAL SPELLS OUT DIVIDEND POLICY.

text.p: Australian financial services group Colonial Ltd on Thursday spelled out its dividend policy and said the make-up of profit, not just its size, could determine the amount paid out to shareholders.

The newly-listed group said it stuck by its prospectus forecast to pay a 6.5 cent dividend if net earnings reached the targeted A$180 million for calendar 1997. It also reiterated its stance that Colonial would strive to distribute about half of net earnings by way of dividends.
But when asked if a higher-than-forecast profit would mean a fatter dividend in 1997, managing director Peter Smedley said this would depend in part on the make-up of profit.
If much of the extra profit came from Asia, which is taken as an unrealised gain on the Asian business's value, Colonial would be less inclined to lift the dividend, the company said.
"We have said we will distribute 50 percent of earnings," said Colonial chief financial officer Tim Wade.
"If, however, Asia represents a disproportionate share of the total, then the distribution would be less than 50 percent," he said.
